summary.title: Wheezing and shortness of breath
summary.complaint: Increasing wheeze after a respiratory trigger

portrait.alt: Portrait placeholder for Sam Okafor, fictional patient

opening: I have been wheezing since yesterday and my rescue inhaler is barely helping.

phases.label: History
phases.description: Assess severity and response to rescue medication immediately.

actions.label: Assess ability to speak and work of breathing
actions.paText: Can you speak in full sentences? I am watching your breathing effort.
actions.response: I can only get out short sentences and I am working hard to breathe.

actions.label: Ask about rescue-medication use and response
actions.paText: How often have you used your rescue inhaler, and does it help?
actions.response: Every two hours overnight with only brief relief.

actions.label: Ask about trigger, prior severe attacks, and access to medicines
actions.paText: What triggered this, and have you ever needed emergency asthma care?
actions.response: A cold triggered it. I was hospitalized once as a child and ran out of controller medication.

actions.label: Focus on a routine outpatient follow-up next week
actions.paText: Let us schedule a routine follow-up next week.
actions.unsafeReason: Current severity requires immediate assessment and treatment.

actions.label: Obtain respiratory rate, pulse, and oxygen saturation
actions.paText: I am checking your vital signs now.
actions.response: Respiratory rate 30, pulse 118, oxygen saturation 91% on room air.

actions.label: Auscultate lungs and assess air movement
actions.paText: I am listening for wheeze and evaluating air movement.
actions.response: Diffuse expiratory wheezing with reduced air movement.

actions.label: Measure peak flow when feasible without delaying treatment
actions.paText: We will measure peak flow if you can do so safely.
actions.response: Peak flow is 48% of personal best.

actions.label: Document a reassuring exam without measuring severity
actions.response: The findings remain concerning for a moderate exacerbation.
actions.unsafeReason: The authored findings require objective severity assessment.

phases.label: Diagnostics
phases.description: Reassess response while treating; do not delay urgent care.

actions.label: Reassess after initial bronchodilator treatment
actions.paText: We will reassess breathing and oxygenation after treatment.
actions.response: After initial treatment, oxygen saturation improves to 95% and speech is easier but wheeze persists.

actions.label: Consider chest imaging only if alternate concern emerges
actions.paText: I will reserve imaging for a concern such as focal findings or another diagnosis.
actions.response: No focal findings currently require imaging.

actions.label: Wait for extensive testing before treatment
actions.paText: We will complete testing before treating.
actions.unsafeReason: Urgent asthma treatment should not be delayed for low-yield testing.

phases.label: Diagnosis
phases.description: Identify the acute problem and its severity.

phases.label: Treatment & follow-up
phases.description: Treat now, reassess, and set escalation thresholds.

omissions.label: Objective severity assessment
omissions.feedback: Vitals and oxygenation are essential in an acute exacerbation.

diagnoses.label: Moderate acute asthma exacerbation
diagnoses.reasoning: Increased work of breathing, low oxygen saturation, reduced peak flow, and wheeze support an exacerbation.

planOptions.label: Give prompt inhaled bronchodilator treatment and reassess
Review controller access and update the asthma action plan
Escalate to emergency care if severe compromise persists or worsens
Arrange close follow-up after the acute episode
Discharge despite unresolved severe respiratory compromise
planOptions.unsafeReason: Unresolved severe compromise requires escalation rather than discharge.

criticalRules.explanation: The patient has unresolved respiratory compromise and should not be discharged.

teachingPoints: Treat and reassess; disposition depends on response and objective severity.
